docs.explain: A plain SUM of a profit-and-loss column tells you the net, which is usually the least useful number in it. Splitting the column by sign with SUMIF gives the two numbers a report actually wants: how much was gained, and how much was lost. The condition is a comparison in quotes, so ">0" keeps the positives and "<0" keeps the negatives, and zero falls in neither bucket — worth remembering, because a zero month disappears from both totals and the two will not add back to the net. The second screen flips the sign of the losses so they read as a size rather than a negative. A leading minus in front of the function does that; it does not change which rows matched, so a mistake in the condition still shows up as the wrong size. If a column can hold text, SUMIF ignores it, but a single SUM over the same range would too — the difference is that SUMIF never adds a row you did not mean to keep.

errors.text: The range holds text that cannot be compared with the number in the condition.
A division by zero in the formula stops it before a total is produced.
The function is misspelled, or SUMIFS was used with SUMIF's argument order.
